ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that A, B, and C are three points on the circle $\odot$O. If $\angle AOB=70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOB=70^\circ$,\\
then $\angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=35^\circ$,\\
therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{35^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Read the figure first: A, B, and C are points on one circle centered at O, with C on the circle and chords CA and CB forming the target angle. Use an analytic unit-circle model instead of quoting the theorem directly. Put O at the origin and take the circle to have radius 1. Rotate coordinates so the radii to A and B have polar angles −35° and +35°, since the central angle AOB is 70°. Let C be any point on the other arc, with polar angle t. For points on the unit circle, the direction of the chord from C at angle t to a point at polar angle α is given by the argument of e^{iα}−e^{it}, whose chord-direction angle differs by half the difference of endpoint polar angles. Thus the angle between chords CA and CB is half the polar-angle separation between A and B: (35°−(−35°))/2 = 35°. Hence ∠ACB = 35°.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached figure shows a circle with center O. Points A, B, and C lie on the circumference: A is on the lower-left part of the circle, B is near the lower-right part, and C is on the right side. The segments OA and OB are drawn as radii, forming the central angle ∠AOB. The chords CA and CB are drawn and meet at C, so the target angle is ∠ACB.

Reasoning: Follow the assigned analytic model. Put O at the origin and take the circle to be the unit circle. Since ∠AOB = 70°, rotate the coordinate system so that A has polar angle -35° and B has polar angle +35°. Thus A = e^{-i35°} and B = e^{i35°}. Let C be any point on the other arc, say C = e^{it}.

For a chord from C = e^{it} to a point P = e^{iα}, its direction vector is e^{iα} - e^{it}. This can be rewritten as e^{iα} - e^{it} = 2i sin((α - t)/2)e^{i(α+t)/2}, so the chord direction angle differs by one half of the endpoint polar-angle difference, up to a possible 180° reversal that does not change the smaller angle between the two chords. Therefore, the angle between chords CA and CB is half the polar-angle separation between A and B:

(35° - (-35°)) / 2 = 70° / 2 = 35°.

So ∠ACB = 35°.
